subject: anaesthesia
title: Acute and chronic pain management: ladders to interventions

steps.tx: Assessment starts with rest, movement, sleep and function **scores**, history by SOCRATES for site and radiation, and DN4 style screening for burning with allodynia that marks **neuropathic** components. Flag cancer, cord compression, fracture and infection as **red flags**, weigh catastrophising and yellow flags, review beliefs, expectations and current drugs with allergies, and map dermatomes with weakness using diaries that link triggers to relief.
steps.say: Assessment is the first step that turns a pain story into a testable plan. Scores at rest, on movement and during sleep are trackers of function over time. SOCRATES is the framework for the history while DN4 screening is the test for burning allodynia of neuropathic pain. Red flags for cancer, cord compression, fracture and infection need same day action. Beliefs, mood and work demands are part of the final plan.

steps.tx: Acute pain follows a stepped **ladder** from paracetamol through anti inflammatory drugs to opioids, scheduled around the clock with **multimodal** layering rather than single agents. Add basal with bolus and lockout **patient controlled analgesia**, thoracic epidural for major abdominal surgery, TAP and rectus catheters, opioid tolerant ketamine infusions, and local wound infusions, then monitor sedation with bowels, trigger pain team escalation, and taper weaning plans at discharge with early physio mobilisation.
steps.say: Acute pain is responsive to scheduled multimodal steps rather than rescue doses alone. Paracetamol with anti inflammatory drugs is the base while opioids are the cover for breakthrough pain. Patient controlled analgesia, epidural and regional catheters are the cover for major surgery. Ketamine helps tolerant patients while wound infusions are added for local control. Sedation charts with bowel plans and pain team triggers keep escalation safe.

vis.alt: A stepped acute pain management ladder, showing paracetamol, NSAIDs, opioid tiers, multimodal strategies, regional blocks, and PCA for effective pain control.
vis.caption: Acute pain management: a stepped approach to multimodal analgesia

steps.tx: Chronic pain splits by mechanism with gabapentin, tricyclic and SNRI tiers for **neuropathic** pain, exercise with manual therapy for back pain, gentle graded activity with sleep care for fibromyalgia, mirror with desensitisation for **complex regional pain**, withdrawal for medication overuse headache, strong opioids with adjuvants for cancer pain, and facet with epidural plus cord **stimulators** for selected refractory cases supported by acceptance and mindfulness psychology with pacing plans.
steps.say: Chronic pain needs mechanism based tiers rather than endless dose rises. Neuropathic pain is responsive to gabapentin, tricyclic and SNRI layers. Back pain is improved with exercise and manual therapy while fibromyalgia is helped with graded activity and sleep care. Complex regional pain is managed with mirror and desensitisation work. Cancer pain is treated with strong opioid tiers with adjuvants and selected cases are referred for facet, epidural or stimulator procedures.

steps.tx: This image shows facet injection needles, epidural needles and dorsal column **stimulator leads** with a generator for refractory pain. The view links facet disease to targeted injection, epidural space to infusion, and dorsal columns to electrical **neuromodulation**. Reserve these **interventions** for selected chronic cases after drugs, exercise and psychology have been optimised with clear functional goals.
steps.say: This image is a display of the procedures behind chronic pain referrals. A facet needle is aimed at small joint pain while an epidural needle is aimed at the spinal space. Dorsal column leads with a generator are modulators of pain signals electrically. These options are suited to selected refractory cases after drugs, exercise and psychology have been tried. Clear functional goals with consent are expected by examiners before any injection.

vis.alt: Lumbar spine showing facet injection needle, epidural needle, and dorsal column stimulator leads with generator.
vis.caption: Spinal facet injection and stimulator leads. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Safety closes every plan with cord, equina and cancer **red flags** acted on the same day, rotation with wean agreements for **tolerance**, screening with brief interventions for **dependence**, co prescribed naloxone for overdose risk, counselling for impairing drugs before driving, fall and constipation guards in the elderly, paracetamol limits in pregnancy, and outcome audits with infection consent for injections while gabapentinoid and benzodiazepine misuse stays watched.
steps.say: Safety decides whether a pain plan can continue. Cord compression, equina syndrome and cancer red flags need same day action. Tolerance is managed with rotation and weaning agreements while dependence is managed with screening and brief help. Overdose risk is met with co prescribed naloxone and driving is counselled for sedating drugs. Elderly patients need fall and constipation checks with regular function review.
